problem:
What is the geometrical interpretation of the transformation represented by the matrix $A$ given below? 

 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

choices.value: A rotation of $\frac{\pi }{4}$ radians counterclockwise about the origin.
A rotation of $\frac{3\pi }{4}$ radians counterclockwise about the origin.
A rotation of $\frac{5\pi }{4}$ radians clockwise about the origin.
A rotation of $\frac{3\pi }{4}$ radians clockwise about the origin.
A rotation of $\frac{\pi }{4}$ radians clockwise about the origin.
